sentences.text: Researchers applied top-down mass spectrometry to analyze tubulin proteins extracted from the brains of wild-type mice and mice with specific gene deletions.
This approach identified 47 distinct tubulin forms, some bearing up to five glutamate residues, which were confirmed using a specific fragmentation technique.
The data indicated that the enzyme TTLL1 adds glutamate chains exclusively to alpha-tubulin, while TTLL7 acts on beta-tubulin.
Deleting either enzyme resulted in a specific reduction of modifications on its target tubulin type, with no compensation from other similar enzymes.
The method enabled rapid identification of these protein variants in complex samples despite the high sequence similarity and acidity of the protein tails.
